Symptoms:
  - This is the resolution/continuation of the SQL-cluster c2/c3/c4 error-40 cascade reported earlier today (see docs/investigations/2026-07-06-dd3912b47506342f.md) — DD metric re-query confirms the full lifecycle: ms-authentication-api and gateway errors continuously elevated 01:24Z→~04:21-04:30Z, then cleanly zero through now (11:09Z). ~3h06m total.
  - Blast radius is wider than the original mid-incident snapshot showed: adds gateway 5xx, method-import-api, nonprod/apps, ms-documents-api, tables-fields, ms-scheduler-api, ms-email-api, method-mobile-notifications-api, and — notably — signup (Growth team, unrelated product surface, pre-account flow).

Signup's Availability SLO monitor (154229727) is still in Alert state (7-day error-budget burn metric, doesn't self-clear on the same timescale as the rest).

Trace IDs: none captured (metric-only re-investigation this cycle, no fresh APM trace pull)
Likely cause: same as the original incident — TCP-reachability loss to SQL clusters c2/c3/c4 (root cause on the SQL/network side still not confirmed by ops)
Suggested next action: ops to confirm SQL/network root cause on clusters c2/c3/c4; once confirmed, finalize kb candidate ki-2026-07-06-sql-cluster-c2c3c4-error40-cascade (proposed, not yet written) — recommend folding signup into that same entry rather than a separate one

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 6)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - Gateway (ms-gateway-api) 4xx-spike monitor fired 10:32:56Z, self-recovered by scan time.
  - Isolated single 30-second burst of 2,883 4xx responses at 10:16:00Z against an otherwise flat 1-3/30s baseline — not a sustained elevation. Out of 62,392 total gateway requests in the 1h40m window.
  - Gateway ships 0 DD Logs entries for the entire day — could not identify the specific route, status code, or client behind the spike. This is a confirmed tooling gap (query ran fine, returned zero), not an "unavailable" placeholder.

Trace IDs: none captured (no logs available for this service today)
Likely cause: undetermined — shape (single sharp isolated spike, self-recovered within one bucket) is most consistent with a brief single-client/bot retry-loop against a route returning 4xx, similar in character to the existing ms-account-api 4xx-spike monitor-noise pattern, but this is a different monitor (first-ever fire) so not filed as a recurrence of that KB entry.
Suggested next action: if this recurs, gateway logging needs to ship to DD Logs before this monitor family can be diagnosed past "spike happened, self-recovered" — worth a defect for that gap independent of this specific alert.

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (SQL cluster c2/c3/c4 connectivity cascade)
Source: #team-incident-response SWAT runbook · critical-path impact · 8+ services
Owning teams (would tag — not tagged): `@admin` (auth/identity/gateway/search), `CRM` (scheduler/rt-core-subscriber), `@no code next gen` (runtime-designer); SQL clusters c2/c3/c4 → infra/DBA

Symptoms:
  • TCP error-40 "Could not open a connection to SQL Server" on sql.connection_c2/c3/c4 from ~01:26–02:18 UTC, cascading 5xx across all SQL-dependent services
  • ms-authentication-api + ms-identity-api (critical path) still elevated at 02:22 UTC — new sessions failing
  • runtime-designer restart (02:17Z) hung on startup, then self-recovered; the SWAT alert scoped it to one host but the root cause is cluster-wide SQL

Likely cause: SQL-tier / network-path reachability loss to clusters c2/c3/c4 (error 40 = TCP-level unreachable, not a deploy). Do NOT keep restarting designercoreapi — it blocks on SQL at startup.
Suggested next action: check SQL hosts backing c2/c3/c4 (up? accepting remote TCP?) + app-tier→SQL-tier network path (SG/firewall/route/DNS ~01:20–01:40Z); prioritize auth/identity over the runtime-designer host.
